mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 645Ci engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement N62B44A engine for a BMW 645Ci typically costs £2,000-£3,500 for a used unit, £3,500-£5,500 for a reconditioned unit, and £5,000-£7,500 for a fully rebuilt engine with a 12-month warranty. Supply and fit adds approximately £780-£1,040 in specialist labour (12-16 hours at £65/hr).

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of N62B44A valve stem seal failure in a 645Ci?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common sign is blue smoke from the exhaust on cold start or after idling, caused by oil seeping past worn valve stem seals into the combustion chamber. Other symptoms include increasing oil consumption between services, fouled spark plugs leading to misfires, and failed MOT emissions tests.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 645Ci?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the condition of the rest of the car. A typical 645Ci is worth £4,000-£12,000. If the body, interior, and transmission are in good condition, a rebuilt engine can extend the car's life by 80,000+ miles and is often cheaper than buying a replacement 645Ci in similar condition.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 645Ci engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most BMW 645Ci engine replacements take 2-4 days for supply and fit at a specialist garage. The N62B44A is a relatively straightforward V8 to remove and refit on the E63/E64 chassis, though the engine bay is tight.

mainEntity.name: Do BMW 645Ci replacement engines come with a warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - all rebuilt and reconditioned BMW 645Ci engines supplied through EnginesMarket include a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Used engines typically have a 3-6 month warranty depending on the supplier. Extended warranty options are available with some specialists.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the 645Ci and 650i engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 645Ci uses the N62B44A - a 4.4-litre V8 producing 333 hp. The 650i uses the N62B48 - a 4.8-litre V8 producing 367 hp. The engines share the same basic architecture, but a 645Ci engine cannot be directly replaced with a 650i engine without significant ECU and hardware changes.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 6 Series 645Ci Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 645Ci is powered exclusively by the N62B44A 4.4-litre V8 - a smooth, powerful engine that's now well into its second decade. While the N62 delivers a refined driving experience, it has several well-documented weak points that become increasingly expensive to manage as mileage climbs. Rebuilt N62B44A engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded valve stem seals, timing chain components, and cooling system parts that address the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Valve Stem Seal Failure - Why the BMW 6 Series 645Ci N62B44A Burns Oil
problems.rootCause: The valve stem seals harden and shrink over time, allowing oil to seep past into the combustion chamber. This leads to blue smoke on start-up, fouled spark plugs, and progressively worsening oil consumption.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace all 32 valve stem seals (labour-intensive - cylinder heads remain on engine)
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if the car is otherwise in good condition and oil consumption is the only issue

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded valve stem seals, timing chain components, water pump, and 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Best for high-mileage engines with multiple concurrent failures

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical BMW 645Ci (2003-2005) in fair-to-good condition is worth approximately £4,000-£12,000 depending on mileage, condition, and whether it's a Coupé or Convertible [THIRD-PARTY - Auto Trader/Parkers market observation]. - Vehicle worth under ~£5,000: valve stem seal replacement or a used engine typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit. - Vehicle worth ~£5,000-£8,000: evaluate both; reconditioned is viable if keeping the car 2+ years. - Vehicle worth ~£8,000-£15,000: reconditioned/rebuilt usually justifies the premium via warranty and reliability. - Vehicle worth £15,000+: replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value.
problems.recommendation: If your 645Ci is burning oil but otherwise running well, have the valve stem seals replaced by a BMW specialist - it's a well-understood job and will restore the engine for many more miles. If the timing chain is rattling or the cooling system has failed, factor in the cumulative cost of repairs: once you're past £3,500 in specialist bills, a rebuilt engine with a warranty starts to look like the better value.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N62B44A BMW 6 Series 645Ci engine prices

problems.h4: Timing Chain Guide Failure - Rattling on Cold Start in the BMW 645Ci
problems.rootCause: The plastic timing chain guides become brittle with age and heat cycling, eventually cracking or breaking. This allows the timing chain to slacken, leading to a rattling noise from the front of the engine - particularly on cold starts.

repairOptions.tier: Timing chain guides and tensioner replacement
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain guides, tensioner, and chain; inspect VANOS units
repairOptions.longevity: Catch it early - before chain skips or breaks

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, new timing chain components, guides, tensioner, VANOS units, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If guides have already failed and caused timing issues

problems.recommendation: A rattling timing chain on a cold start is a warning sign - don't ignore it. If caught early, replacing the guides and tensioner is a viable repair. If the chain has skipped or the engine has lost timing, a full rebuilt engine is typically the most cost-effective solution, as the repair bill for a damaged cylinder head often exceeds the value of the car.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N62B44A BMW 6 Series 645Ci engine prices

problems.h4: Cooling System Failure - Electric Water Pump and Thermostat in the BMW 645Ci
problems.rootCause: The N62 uses an electric water pump rather than a belt-driven mechanical unit. These electric pumps fail without much warning, leading to rapid overheating. The thermostat can also stick, exacerbating temperature regulation issues.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace electric water pump, thermostat, and coolant
repairOptions.longevity: Preventative - do this before it fails

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, includes new water pump, thermostat, upgraded cooling components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If overheating has already caused head gasket or block damage

problems.recommendation: The electric water pump on the N62B44A is a known weak point - replace it preventatively at around 80,000 miles if you're keeping the car. It's far cheaper than a overheated engine. If your 645Ci has already overheated, get a compression test done immediately; if the head gasket is compromised, a rebuilt engine is the safest route.
